engine/dag_navigator.py:R5:DAGNavigator:: R5 `isinstance(plugin, GateSettings)` inside the `_fork_gate_node_ids` frozenset comprehension over `node_to_plugin.items()`. GateSettings is a concrete dataclass ELSPETH defines (`core/config.py`), and `node_to_plugin` is typed `Mapping[NodeID, RowPlugin | GateSettings]` and built by graph_wiring from config.transforms + config.gates only, so this is ADR-032 nominal typing of an owned closed union, not structural typing of a foreign shape. The comprehension is a pure one-shot topology projection computed at construction; the alternative (asking each plugin whether it is a gate) would re-measure conformance on a Protocol, which is the failure ef5e6e593 and elspeth-8783933d99 both record. A gate misclassified here is silently absent from `_fork_gate_node_ids` for the life of the navigator, so every later fork-membership query answers wrongly with no error. INVALIDATED BY: a third plugin kind entering `node_to_plugin`; GateSettings becoming an ABC/Protocol with several concrete carriers; or gate identity moving onto a declared field, at which point the dispatch should read that field instead of the type.

R5 `isinstance(plugin, GateSettings)` as the positive arm of a deliberately NEGATIVE dispatch: gate -> set `encountered_gate`, everything else -> treat as a transform and read `plugin.on_success`. The in-code comment records why (elspeth-8783933d99): the previous version measured TransformProtocol conformance on the else arm, which silently skipped non-conforming transforms and mis-resolved the jump-target sink. Testing the one owned concrete class and taking the complement is the ratified fix, and gates specifically MUST be detected because a gate self-routes at execution time — the walk returns None rather than a statically resolved sink, so missing a gate here would bind a jump target to a sink the gate was going to override. INVALIDATED BY: `node_to_plugin` admitting a third kind that is neither gate nor transform (the else arm would then read `on_success` off it and mis-resolve); or gates acquiring a static `on_success` that the walk should honour.
engine/executors/gate.py:R5:GateExecutor: R5 `isinstance(eval_result, str)` — second arm of the same route-label conversion, reached only when the value is not a bool. A str result IS the route label verbatim and is immediately re-validated against the configured routes (`if route_label not in gate_config.routes: raise ValueError`), so an accepted str cannot reach routing without a configured destination. Narrowing here is required rather than optional because the label is row-derived, untrusted text: it is used as a dict key against `gate_config.routes` and echoed into the ConfigGateReason audit record, and both uses need the value proven to be a str first. Same J-not-D reasoning as the bool arm — `eval_result` is not rooted at a parameter of this function. INVALIDATED BY: route labels becoming a closed enum or NewType validated at the parser boundary (this check then moves there); or the unconfigured-label ValueError below being removed, which would let an arbitrary row-derived string reach destination resolution.

R5 `isinstance(eval_result, bool)` — first arm of the route-label conversion for the value returned by `ExpressionParser.evaluate()` (declared `-> Any`). The bool arm must be tested FIRST and separately because a bool maps to the reserved 'true'/'false' route labels, not to its string form. The project data manifesto forbids `bool(result)` coercion on pipeline data, so the type has to be asserted rather than coerced. This is J and not D: `eval_result` is genuinely Tier-3 row-derived data, but it is produced INSIDE `execute_config_gate` rather than arriving through one of its parameters, so `@trust_boundary(source_param=...)` cannot honestly root the flagged subject and the decorator would be a whole-function exemption cloak. The chain does not fall through silently: the terminal else raises TypeError carrying only bounded, scrubbed metadata via `_describe_untrusted_gate_value`. INVALIDATED BY: the evaluator acquiring a declared narrow return type (the check becomes redundant); a third supported route-value type added without extending both this chain and the `gate_config.routes` lookup; or the terminal `raise TypeError` being removed or softened so an unsupported value routes silently.
engine/executors/transform.py:R5:Transfo: R5 `isinstance(transform, BatchTransformRuntimeProtocol)` selecting the row-pipelined batch runtime. FLAGGING A KNOWN DEFECT, NOT DEFENDING THE PATTERN: `BatchTransformRuntimeProtocol` (`contracts/batch_runtime.py:18`) is `@runtime_checkable`, so this is structural typing used as a dispatch control, which ADR-032 and AGENTS.md disallow — an impostor with the right member names passes, and adding a member to the protocol would silently de-classify the sole real implementer (`BatchTransformMixin`, `plugins/infrastructure/batching/mixin.py:41`, the only definer of `batch_runtime_enabled` in the tree). That is precisely the ef5e6e593 mode the sibling dispatch in `engine/token_traversal.py` documents. It is justified rather than fixed HERE because every honest fix leaves this lane's file set: dispatching nominally on `BatchTransformMixin` would make `engine/` import from `plugins/` (today `engine/` has zero such imports), and introducing an owned concrete base in `contracts/` edits another wave-1 lane's files. The blast radius is bounded and fail-soft in the safe direction: a false negative yields `batch_runtime = None` and the transform runs row-wise, and the conjunct `transform.batch_runtime_enabled` means an impostor still has to opt in. Follow-up ticket owed to replace this with a nominal owned base. INVALIDATED BY: a second implementer of the protocol; any new member added to `BatchTransformRuntimeProtocol` (silently disables batch runtime for every existing transform); or the arrival of an owned concrete base class that `engine/` may legitimately import — at which point this must become a nominal check, not a renewed exception.

R5 `isinstance(e, TimeoutError)` on an exception already bound by `except Exception as e:`. TimeoutError is a concrete stdlib class, so this is nominal discrimination, not shape probing. It cannot be replaced by a dedicated `except TimeoutError` arm without duplicating or reordering the common terminal-audit sequence this handler owns — `_verify_ownership_before_terminal_audit(guard)` then `guard.complete(FAILED, error=...)` must run identically for every failure before any timeout-specific action. The narrowed arm performs exactly one side-effect, `batch_runtime.evict_submission(...)`, which frees the reorder-buffer slot so a retry is not FIFO-blocked, and then the handler re-raises; it records no audit evidence and changes no outcome, so a mis-discrimination degrades retry throughput rather than fabricating or suppressing audit facts. The `batch_runtime is not None` conjunct means the arm is inert for non-batch transforms. INVALIDATED BY: the handler ceasing to re-raise (the arm would then decide a terminal outcome); eviction acquiring audit side-effects; or a plugin timeout type that does not derive from TimeoutError needing the same eviction, which would make this check silently incomplete.
engine/token_traversal.py:R5:TokenTraver: R5 `isinstance(gate_outcome, _GateTerminal)` narrowing `_GateOutcome = _GateContinue | _GateTerminal` (`token_traversal.py:105`), a two-arm union of module-private frozen slotted dataclasses defined in this same file and returned only by `handle_gate_node`. Both arms are consumed here and they carry disjoint fields: `_GateTerminal.result` is returned to the caller immediately, while `_GateContinue` carries the `updated_token`/`updated_sink`/`next_node_id` continuation state the loop then advances on. Narrowing the wrong way either drops a terminal RowResult (the token vanishes from the run) or reads continuation fields that do not exist on the terminal arm. The union is private to this module, so no external implementer can widen it and isinstance cannot be defeated by an impostor. INVALIDATED BY: a third arm added to `_GateOutcome`; either arm gaining a shared discriminant field (dispatch should then read the field); or the union being exported so foreign types could inhabit it.

R5 `isinstance(transform_outcome, _TransformTerminal)` narrowing `_TransformOutcome = _TransformContinue | _TransformTerminal` (`token_traversal.py:86`), the transform-side twin of the gate outcome union: module-private frozen slotted dataclasses returned only by `handle_transform_node`. Same disjoint-field argument — the terminal arm's `result` is returned immediately (and may be a `tuple[RowResult, ...]` for de-aggregation fan-out, ADR-020), the continue arm supplies `updated_token`/`updated_sink` for the next hop. This site sits in the `else` (transform) arm of the plugin dispatch, so it runs once per transform node per token; a wrong narrowing here loses or duplicates row results in the run's terminal accounting. INVALIDATED BY: a third arm added to `_TransformOutcome`; a discriminant field being added; or the union leaving module scope.

R5 `isinstance(plugin, GateSettings)` — the plugin dispatch of the inner traversal loop, and the positive arm of a deliberately negative dispatch whose else arm is the transform. `plugin is None` (structural nodes such as coalesce) is handled and `continue`d immediately above, so the value here is the closed owned union `RowPlugin | GateSettings`, built by graph_wiring from config.transforms + config.gates, which raises on anything else. The in-code comment records why conformance is NOT measured on the transform arm: widening the runtime_checkable TransformProtocol de-classified every implementation missing the new member and the dispatch raise fired mid-traversal (ef5e6e593, elspeth-8783933d99, ADR-032 addendum). Testing the single owned concrete class is what makes this dispatch nominal. INVALIDATED BY: `node_to_plugin` gaining a third plugin kind (the else arm would then run it as a transform); graph_wiring ceasing to raise on unknown kinds; or GateSettings gaining concrete subclasses that must dispatch differently.
engine/triggers.py:R5:TriggerEvaluator:_: R5 `not isinstance(result, bool)` guarding the value returned by `ExpressionParser.evaluate()` (declared `-> Any`), raising TypeError on anything else. This is a Tier-1 crash-on-anomaly integrity guard, not a Tier-3 boundary parse, so `@trust_boundary` is a category error here — the decorator rejects tier != 3 by construction. The in-code comment cites the standing prohibition on `if bool(result)` coercion for our data: a truthy non-bool (a non-empty string, a numpy.bool_, a count) would silently decide an aggregation barrier. AT THIS SITE (`_replay_condition_over_members`): the guard runs inside the prefix replay that reconstructs the durable latch after an out-of-order member insert or an anchor rewind. The first prefix whose condition is true becomes the returned fire instant, so a coerced truthy value does not merely fire early — it backdates the durable latch to the wrong member arrival time and the function returns that instant as fact. Crashing is correct: the replay is a pure function of durable state and has no defensible fallback. INVALIDATED BY: a declared bool return contract on the evaluator; or the replay becoming best-effort rather than authoritative for the durable latch.
